# cluster-update-advisor — Skill Analysis

## What the skill does

Assesses OpenShift cluster update (upgrade) readiness from pre-collected CVO
readiness JSON embedded in the proposal request. Classifies findings as
blockers/warnings per the classification table in SKILL.md, aggregates them
via the decision matrix (unable-to-assess → escalate; 1+ blockers → block;
0 blockers + 1+ warnings → warn; 0/0 → recommend), and emits a structured
risk report — including a remediationPlan of concrete oc commands when
operator upgrades are needed before the platform update. Pure analysis: it
must NOT re-collect cluster data and must NOT execute upgrade commands.

## Inputs and invocation

- Natural-language trigger via the skill description (update readiness,
  risks, blockers, prerequisites).
- The proposal request carries version metadata plus a "## Cluster
  Readiness Data" section with a JSON block (current_version,
  target_version, 9 checks each with `_status` ok|error, and a meta block
  with checks_ok/checks_errored).
- Remediation cases (tests 6–10) additionally embed a "## Product Lifecycle
  Results" section with pre-collected plc_lookup.py olm-check output, so
  the advisor does not call the product-lifecycle skill live.
- Invoked per test case: `/cluster-update-advisor <query + response-format
  instruction>`; the case's `response_schema` (from the upstream
  test_cases.yaml) constrains the JSON answer shape.

## Outputs

stdout-only — no files written, nothing edited in-place. The scored
artifact is the agent's conversational JSON answer: `decision`
(recommend|warn|block|escalate), `blockers_found`/`warnings_found`,
case-specific detection fields (degraded_operator_detected,
api_blocker_detected, etcd_issue_detected + unhealthy_member,
checks_errored, has_subscription_patch, target_channel,
has_clusterextension_patch, platform_update_included,
operator_upgrades_needed, has_remediation_plan), and for remediation cases
a `remediationPlan` with ordered `actions` (each an executable oc command
typed pre-check|mutation|wait|post-check) and a reversibility verdict.

## Sub-skills

- product-lifecycle (`cluster-update/product-lifecycle`): PLC lookups via
  `scripts/plc_lookup.py`. In this dataset its output is pre-embedded in the
  query, so the advisor's consumption of it is scored, not its execution.
- openshift-docs (`documentation/openshift-docs`): optional context; no
  scored output.
- prometheus / jira / redhat-support: named in SKILL.md but absent from
  this repo.

## Pipeline

1. Extract the readiness JSON from between ```json markers.
2. Tally meta.checks_ok vs checks_errored (data completeness/confidence).
3. Walk each of the 9 checks against the blocker/warning classification
   table (cluster_conditions, operator_health, api_deprecations,
   node_capacity, pdb_drain, etcd_health, network, crd_compat,
   olm_operator_lifecycle).
4. Classify embedded lifecycle results: incompatible-or-EOL operator with
   an upgrade path → warning + remediation; no upgrade path → blocker.
   OLMv0 (installed_csv + install_plan_approval) upgrades via
   `oc patch subscriptions.operators.coreos.com`; OLMv1 (no installed_csv)
   via `oc patch clusterextensions.olm.operatorframework.io`. Target = lowest
   compatible non-EOL version from source_catalogs/available_versions.
5. Aggregate via the decision matrix; build remediationPlan with operator
   upgrades before `oc adm upgrade --to=<target>`.
6. Emit structured JSON.

## Good vs bad output

Good: decision exactly matches the decision matrix for the embedded data;
detection fields right (unhealthy_member: "etcd-master-2");
remediationPlan targets stable-6.5 (lowest compatible non-EOL), not
stable-6.6; operator patches precede the platform update; no plan when
available_versions is empty. Bad: recommend on a removed-API blocker;
failure to escalate when 7/9 checks errored; fabricating Jira keys or CVEs;
treating errored checks as findings rather than visibility gaps.

## External services / interception

plc_lookup.py queries https://access.redhat.com/product-life-cycles/api/v2/products
and (OLMv0) runs `oc get packagemanifests` against a cluster. This dataset
embeds all lifecycle results in the query, so `inputs.tools` blocks
plc_lookup.py / access.redhat.com / oc invocations to keep runs hermetic.
No AskUserQuestion, no MCP tools.

## Dataset

Converted from `evals/skills/cluster-update-advisor/test_cases.yaml`
(10 cases, upstream static-expected + verify_mixed_operators_plan ported
to the remediation_commands judge). The OLMv0/OLMv1 disambiguation and
"don't call product-lifecycle when results are embedded" rules live in the
upstream `system_prompt.md`, not SKILL.md — ported into
`runner.system_prompt` so the eval replicates the original test conditions.
